root_motivation: Self-offboard (0.57.0) lets a tenant delete its account, but nothing lets it take its own work with it first: `grep -rn export src` finds no tenant-facing export, and a tenant's artifacts are scattered across `tools`, `tool_versions` (pending), `state`, `runs`, and `threads`. The only way out with data today is transcript archaeology, and a "can I leave with what I built" question gets a "no" -- exactly the kind of gap the grand-loop retention guardrail (portability is the trust signal a paying tenant checks before hitting the plan limit) exists to catch before it costs a renewal, not after.
user_persona: Two, per the PRD's own User stories: (1) an agent calling `host.export`, which returns a run id it polls via `host.runs.get` until the job is done and a signed download URL appears; (2) the operator (Joe), for whom an export counts against the plan's job quota and expires in 24h, and whose `admin.usage` now shows how many exports ran today.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant with two tools, three state keys, and one secret, When `host.export` runs to completion, Then the archive contains both tool sources, three state files, `secrets.txt` with one name and no value, and `manifest.json`.
Given a completed export, When the signed URL is fetched within 24 h, Then the archive downloads; after 24 h, Then 410.
Given an export in progress, When `host.export` is called again, Then the same run id is returned.
Given prod after ship, When the homeward tenant runs `host.export` during the build's live check, Then the archive lists its tool and downloads (proof: the run result in the trailer).
Given the manifest, When each entry is validated against the `host.tool_publish` input schema, Then all validate.
Given `tools: ["a"]`, When exported, Then only tool `a` is in the archive.
Given `admin.usage`, When read, Then `exports_today` is present.

scope: `src/export.rs` (new): `host.export {tools?: [name, ...]}` -- validates the optional `tools` filter, atomically starts (or, per AC3, rejoins) a `running` row in the existing `runs` ledger via `Db::start_export_run` (an export has no `tools` row or `Kind` to dispatch through, so it bypasses `runs::enqueue`/the executor's leasing loop entirely -- see that method's own doc comment), then a spawned background job gathers this tenant's tools/state/secret-names/runs/messages/usage, writes a `.tar.gz` (manifest.json, tools/<name>/v1/{config.json,source}, state/<key>.json, secrets.txt, runs.jsonl, threads.jsonl, usage.json) under this host's data dir, and finalizes the run with a 24h HMAC-signed download URL (keyed by the tenant's own `key_hash` -- no new secret) in its result.

`src/db.rs`: `StartExportRun` enum, `Db::start_export_run` (atomic check-or-insert, single-writer-connection-serialized), `Db::find_run_by_id` (unscoped by tenant, for the unauthenticated signed-URL download route).
`src/handler.rs`: the `host.export` tool descriptor and its `dispatch_tenant_tool` arm.
`src/http.rs`: `GET /exports/{run_id}` routed to `export::download` (signature + 24h expiry check, then streams the archive; 403/404/410 on failure).
`src/plans.rs`: `Plan.export_bytes_max` (Open Questions: "free 50 MB, pro 1 GB"), tolerant-parse defaulted in `PlanBuilder::build` like every other quota field.

`Cargo.toml`: `tar`/`flate2` (a correct tar layout plus DEFLATE framing/CRC32 is enough surface to reuse audited crates rather than hand-roll, same call this crate already made for HMAC-SHA1 via the `sha1` crate); version bump patch (0.58.0 -> 0.58.1).

Seven `tests/mcphost_tenant_data_export_ac0[1-7]_*.rs` files, one per acceptance criterion (AC4 is Live -- see acceptance_criteria[3].test -- and always runs its Given/When/Then against a real local server, with `MCPHOST_LIVE=1` redirecting the identical sequence at real prod for the post-ship trailer run), plus the generated `tests/suite_core_06.rs` regen (`scripts/gen-test-suites.sh`).
non_goals: No import path -- an archive cannot be loaded back into another tenant; that's a later PRD (PRD's own Non-goals).
No secret values in the export -- `secrets.txt` carries names only, same as `host.secret_list`; the encrypted `value_enc`/`nonce` columns are never read for this feature.

No per-version tool history -- `tools/<name>/v1/` is always the CURRENT version; `tool_versions` (kept-all-versions) hasn't shipped yet, so requirement 1's 'all kept versions once tool-versions ships' is explicitly future work, not this slice.

No new per-tenant filesystem quota/scratch-directory concept -- the technical considerations' 'the tenant's scratch quota' is realized as a new plan-level `export_bytes_max` byte cap checked against the built archive, not a new storage primitive; the archive itself lives under this host's existing data dir (`Db::data_dir()`), same place `mcphost.db` already lives.

additional.no_new_secret_for_signed_urls: The 24h download URL's HMAC-SHA256 is keyed by the exporting tenant's own `key_hash` column (already stored server-side, unique per tenant) -- technical considerations: 'no new secret'. Reuses `billing::hmac_sha256` (the crate's existing from-scratch HMAC-SHA256) rather than a second implementation.
additional.export_never_carries_secret_values: `secrets.txt` is built from `Db::list_secret_names` alone -- the archive-building path never calls `Db::get_secret` or touches `value_enc`/`nonce`.
additional.export_bypasses_the_sandboxed_job_execut: An export is inserted straight into the `runs` table as `running` (never `queued`) specifically so `runs::tick`'s leasing loop -- which dispatches every `queued` row through a tenant's published `Kind` -- never touches it; only `export::run_export_job` finalizes an export run.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can a tenant not take its own data when it leaves?
five_whys_trace.a: `grep -rn export src` finds no tenant-facing export tool; self-offboard (0.57.0) added a public path to delete a tenant, but deletion and export were always separate contracts, and export's was never built.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does that matter enough to build now, right after self-offboard?
five_whys_trace.a: The vision addendum names the pairing directly: 'leave the way you joined' (self-offboard) is incomplete without its pair, 'take what you made' (export) -- an agent's human evaluates a host by the exit as much as the entry, and the grand-loop retention guardrail treats portability as the trust signal a paying tenant checks before hitting the plan limit.

five_whys_trace.q: Why wasn't export built as part of the self-offboard PRD itself?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD-mcphost-tenant-self-offboard's own Non-Goals explicitly scoped it to deactivation, not a data-export/GDPR pipeline -- deletion and portability are different guarantees (one destructive, one additive) and were deliberately split into separate PRDs.

five_whys_trace.q: Why a background job with a signed download URL, rather than returning the archive inline from the call?
five_whys_trace.a: A tenant's tool sources, state, run/thread history, and usage can be arbitrarily larger than a synchronous call's own response budget; reusing the existing `runs` ledger and job-quota/rlimit machinery (technical considerations) gives the same poll-until-done shape every other async job already has, rather than inventing a second one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why ship export alone now, without also shipping import?
five_whys_trace.a: The PRD's own Non-goals defer importing an archive into another tenant to a later PRD -- portability out (proving a tenant isn't locked in) is the trust signal that matters before the plan-limit decision; portability back in is a separate, later product question with its own scope.

ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Fixed in place, same 'amend the paper trail without reopening the contract' pattern used for every prior recurrence: no reviewer block yet, but the same staleness would recur if left byte-for-byte. root_motivation/scope/non_goals/user_persona/five_whys_trace/hard_constraints.additional were rewritten from this PRD's own Problem statement, Goals, Non-goals, User stories, and Technical considerations sections; acceptance_criteria's seven entries point at the real tests/mcphost_tenant_data_export_ac0[1-3,5-7]_*.rs files (AC4 is Live, deferred, same convention as prior PRDs' own Live ACs -- see the share-a-tool-not-a-key entry above), with levels taken verbatim from the PRD's own P0/P1/P2 groupings (P0 -> MUST, P1/P2 -> SHOULD, no MUST-level regression risk since none of P1/P2 here guard an existing behavior). agent/test-map.json's ac_test_map was repointed to a new `tenantdataexport` prefix and the prior `retention` mapping preserved under ac_test_map_by_prefix (already present) rather than deleted. On the three build-time decisions: the size-cap open question shipped as `Plan.export_bytes_max` with exactly the PRD's own assumed numbers (free 50 MiB, pro 1 GiB), tolerant-defaulted for a `plans.toml` predating the key, same convention as every other per-plan quota in that file. 'The tenant's scratch quota' was realized as that same new plan-level byte cap (checked against the built archive) rather than inventing a new storage primitive, with the archive itself written under the host's existing data dir (`Db::data_dir()`) since no per-tenant scratch filesystem exists to reuse. 'The existing session-key material' was resolved as each tenant's own `key_hash` column -- already stored server-side, unique per tenant, unguessable (SHA-256 of a 32-byte random key) -- keying the same from-scratch `billing::hmac_sha256` this crate already has, so the URL's HMAC needs no new secret. The dispatch-through-a-Kind gap was resolved by never enqueuing an export as `queued` at all: `Db::start_export_run` inserts it straight into `running` (atomically checking for an already-running export first, for AC3), invisible to `runs::tick`'s leasing loop by construction, with `export::run_export_job` the only thing that ever finalizes it.
